authorization: etymologise remaining Indo-Aryan surveys. do not rebuild. work autonomously and do what you can, you have 8 hours, i will review once your time is done.

proposals.evidence: Turner identifies Hindi gayā, Nepali/Kumaoni gayo and Old Gujarati gyau/giu as suppletive preterites of go from gata. These survey gV(y)- forms preserve that gone/past stem even though the elicitation gloss is simply go. Forms retaining an l expansion are assigned to the separate *gatailla branch.

proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly separates the illa extension of gata: Prakrit gaïllaya, Assamese gâla, Bengali gela, Oriya gali/gelā, Bihari gel and Bhojpuri gail. These survey g-l past go forms match that extension, with ordinary agreement vowels and local vowel reduction. The Danuwar records are explicitly tagged third-person singular preterite; none is treated as a present yāti stem.

proposals.evidence: Turner gives Prakrit sutta asleep, Old Gujarati sūtaü and Bhojpuri sūtal under supta, distinguishing this t-bearing past/asleep stem from the present svap-/sup- series. Vasavi huṭalo retains the corresponding t-plus-l form, with western s-to-h and the survey’s retroflex spelling. The link is to the participial sleep family; it does not claim an independently demonstrated history for every local suffix.
